test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 31 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Of the residents of a housing society, (13)/(18) own cars and among those who own cars, (48)/(65) have purchased cubby parking space. If 136 residents park in the open, then how many total residents live in the society?
solution:
Given:

Fraction of residents who own cars = 13/18

Fraction of car owners who purchased cubby parking space = 48/65

Residents parking in the open = 136

Formula used:

Residents parking in the open = Residents owning cars - Residents with cubby parking

Calculation:

Let the total number of residents be N.

Residents who own cars = (13/18) × N

Residents with cubby parking = (48/65) × [(13/18) × N]

Residents parking in the open = Residents who own cars - Residents with cubby parking:

136 = [(13/18) × N] - [(48/65) × (13/18) × N]

⇒ 136 = (13N / 18) × [1 - (48/65)]

⇒ 136 = (13N / 18) × (17/65)

⇒ 136 = (221N / 1170)

⇒ N = (136 × 1170) / 221

⇒ N = 720

∴ The total number of residents in the society is 720, which corresponds to option 3.
